method:rack::componentlibrary::LightSlid.finding: P2: the implementation and test are fine (_componentlibrary.py LightSlider.step mirrors Rack; test_light_sliders_and_buttons asserts the light's centre x). The record metadata and docs are off. (1) `callback` is null (manifest.json:2028), but this is a Python override that Rack's UI step calls through the widget trampoline, and Widget::step is recorded as callback "ui" (manifest.json:2777). (2) The cited docs (componentlibrary.md#cl-templates) never describe step: the light following the handle centre. Smallest fix: set callback to "ui" and add one sentence on step to the cl-templates section.

method:rack::componentlibrary::Rectangle.finding: P2: the Python body matches Rack's RectangleLight::drawBackground and is dispatched by app.cpp:214. Two problems remain. (1) `callback` is null (manifest.json:2029), though Rack's UI draw calls this Python function; LightWidget::drawBackground is recorded as callback "ui" (manifest.json:1719). (2) test_rectangle_lights_draw_with_racks_code samples pixel (5,3) of a 10x6 light (test_components.py:221-228). Rack's default circular LightWidget::drawBackground (radius 3 centred at (3,3), src/app/LightWidget.cpp:30-33) also covers that pixel up to anti-aliasing, so the test only tells rectangle from circle by a 0.05 px AA margin. Smallest fix: set callback "ui" and also assert a corner pixel such as (9,0) or (9,5).

P2: the Python body matches Rack's RectangleLight::drawLight and is dispatched by app.cpp:218. Two problems remain. (1) `callback` is null (manifest.json:2030), though LightWidget::drawLight is recorded as "ui" (manifest.json:1722) and this is the same UI-thread Python dispatch. (2) The layer-1 check samples pixel (5,3) (test_components.py:229-236), which also lies within Rack's default circle of radius 3 at (3,3) (src/app/LightWidget.cpp:50-58). The test therefore does not deliberately prove rectangular drawing. Smallest fix: set callback "ui" and assert a pixel outside the inscribed circle, such as (9,3).

method:rack::componentlibrary::SegmentDi.finding: P1: the binding is correct (behavior.hpp:51-62 calls cl::SegmentDisplay::draw). But the cited assertion `pixel(image, 0, 0)[:3] == (0, 0, 0)` (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py ~line 299) cannot fail: Rack's FramebufferWidget clears to transparent black (src/widget/FramebufferWidget.cpp:296, glClearColor(0,0,0,0)), so an undrawn background also gives RGB (0,0,0). The cited docs (componentlibrary.md#cl-components) also don't mention draw or the black background. Smallest fix: assert `pixel(image, 0, 0) == (0, 0, 0, 255)`, and add 'draw() paints Rack's black background, then the segments' to the SegmentDisplay bullet.

method_template:rack::componentlibrary::.finding: P2: _set_lights (src/rackpy/raw/_componentlibrary.py) is a line-for-line, faithful Python version of Rack's setLights<TLightBase> (componentlibrary.hpp SegmentDisplay::setLights). But test_segment_display (tests/app/in_rack/test_components.py:287-300) checks only the count, type, module and first_light_id. It never checks the reimplemented segment geometry (pos/size from margin and r) or the vertical branch, so a geometry error would not fail any test. Smallest fix: assert lights[i].box.pos.x == pytest.approx(i/3*(30-m)+m) and size.x == pytest.approx((30-m)/3-m), then repeat with display.vertical = True.
